transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um... I'm here because, well, I just feel like I'm always running hot. It's like... I can't shut the motor off, you know? And lately, that's been getting me into some trouble at the firehouse. So I figured it was time to come in and talk to somebody about it.
Do you ever have distinct periods where you feel unusually energized or euphoric compared with your normal self?

No, I wouldn't say that. It's not like... well, it doesn't really come in phases or anything. I don't get periods where I feel super happy or on top of the world. It's more just... like I said, I'm always kind of wired. That's just my normal every day, not some special mood that suddenly hits me.
Since you were a child, have you often had trouble sitting still?

Yeah, pretty much for as long as I can remember. Even now, if I’m sitting in a meeting at the station... my leg is just constantly bouncing. I’ll be clicking a pen, shifting around in the chair, or just messing with whatever happens to be in front of me. I honestly do it without even noticing it most of the time.
Do you often have trouble staying focused on a task, even when you want to?

Yeah, definitely. It happens a lot. Like, if we're in a briefing at the station, or doing drone training... I'll be totally locked in for the first few minutes. But then I'll suddenly realize I've just been staring at the map, or the screen, and I didn't catch half of what command just said. It's frustrating because I really am trying to pay attention, but my focus just kind of drifts off without me even realizing it.
Do these focus and restlessness problems cause difficulties for you outside of work too?

Yeah, it definitely causes some issues at home, but... honestly, the biggest problem right now is what it's doing to me at work. It’s actually started costing me trust at the firehouse. I just got pulled into a performance and safety meeting about it recently. I’ve been working toward moving into leadership, but now it feels like that shot is slipping away. The crew just feels like they can’t count on me to track the details consistently, and in our line of work, that's a really big deal.
Do you often act before thinking?

I don't really think so. I mean... I might lose track of details, but I don't usually just jump into things without thinking. Especially on the job, we train to react fast, but it's not like I'm making rash decisions or doing things on impulse. So, no, I haven't really noticed that being an issue for me.
Have you been through a traumatic event that you feel these problems started after?

No, I wouldn't say so. I mean, being a firefighter, I've seen some bad things, sure. We go on calls that are tough to deal with. But... I don't feel like there was one specific event that triggered all this. These issues with focus and keeping track of things, they've been around for a long time. It's not a new thing that just started after a bad call or anything like that.
When you're trying to relax, do you still feel restless and unable to settle down?

Yeah, I definitely do. Even on my days off, I have a really hard time just... doing quiet stuff with my family. Like, if we're trying to watch a movie or just hang out, I can't seem to just sit there. I start talking, or I'm moving around, or I'll suddenly decide I need to go check on the tools in the garage. I almost always end up getting up before I've even been sitting for very long. It's just hard to actually settle down.
Do you spend a lot of time worrying excessively about different parts of your life?

No, not really. I mean, I have the normal stress that comes with the job and providing for my family, but... I wouldn't say I spend a lot of time just sitting around worrying about things. It's more that my mind is always going a mile a minute about what I need to *do*, rather than worrying about what's going to happen, if that makes sense.
